theme: 3 terms on operators: updating a variable in place, giving plus a new meaning, and creating a brand-new operator

terms.definition: An operator, such as plus-equals, that does math on a variable and stores the result back in it.
terms.example: Just use a Compound Assignment Operator: `count += 1`.

terms.definition: A feature that gives an existing operator, such as plus, a new meaning for your own type.
terms.example: With Operator Overloading, we can add two `Point` values with a plus sign.

terms.definition: A feature that lets you declare a brand-new operator symbol and decide what it does.
terms.example: Please don't add a Custom Operator here, a named method is easier to read.

video.description:
Learn to explain operators on your own types in Swift: Compound Assignment Operator, Operator Overloading & Custom Operator, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Compound Assignment Operator - An operator, such as plus-equals, that does math on a variable and stores the result back in it.
Operator Overloading - A feature that gives an existing operator, such as plus, a new meaning for your own type.
Custom Operator - A feature that lets you declare a brand-new operator symbol and decide what it does.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain these operator terms in English?

dialogue.title: Why didn't += compile?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `+=` didn't compile for `Money`, but `+` worked. Why?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You wrote Operator Overloading for `+` only. `+=` needs its own function.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Really? I thought a Compound Assignment Operator came for free.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not for your own types. So I added `+=` with an `inout` parameter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because a Compound Assignment Operator changes `total` itself?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The result goes back into `total`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cool. Can I make a Custom Operator for tips too, like plus-percent?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You can, but a Custom Operator is hard to read for new teammates.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So a method like `addTip` is clearer?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Usually. Keep Operator Overloading for obvious math, like money.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Operator Overloading for clear math, a Compound Assignment Operator for updates, and a Custom Operator rarely.
